data.name: Nandana
data.long_meaning: The name Nandana is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘nandana’, which means ‘giver of delight’ or ‘garden of joy’. In Hindu mythology, Nandana is the name of the celestial garden created by Lord Indra, where the gods reside. It is also the name of Lord Shiva's consort, Parvati, who is known as the embodiment of pure love and joy.

This name is a reminder of the inner happiness and joy that one can derive from the union of the self with the divine. It also serves as a reminder to seek joy and happiness within, rather than relying on external sources. Furthermore, Nandana represents the divine garden of life, which is full of blessings from the gods, and is a constant source of inspiration, growth, and nourishment.
